listen.script: Good morning, students. There is a small change to tomorrow's science trip to the museum. The bus was going to leave at eight o'clock, but because of traffic on the main road, it will now leave at half past eight. Please remember to bring your own lunch, because the museum café is closed for repairs this week.
listen.q: Why do the students need to bring their own lunch?
options: Because the trip will take longer than usual
Because the museum café is closed
Because the bus is leaving later

listen.script: Noura: Shall we buy Grandma some flowers for Eid? Sara: Hmm, she already has lots of flowers in her garden. I think she'd prefer a book. She finished the last story I gave her in two days! Noura: That's true. But she's been talking about trying new recipes, so let's get her a cookbook this time. Sara: Perfect, let's do that.
listen.q: What are the girls going to buy for their grandmother?

read.passage: Last month, our class started a project to help our neighbourhood. At first, I wasn't very excited because I thought it would be boring. Our teacher, Mr Saleh, asked us to choose one problem to solve. We noticed that the small park near our school was full of rubbish, and younger children couldn't play there safely. Every Saturday morning, ten of us met at the park with bags and gloves. After three weeks, the park looked completely different. Some parents even brought new plants and helped us put them in the ground. Now I walk past the park every day and feel proud. I've learned that small actions can make a big difference.

qs.q: How did the writer feel about the project at the beginning?
options: He was not very interested in it
He was worried about the younger children

qs.q: What did some parents do to help?
options: They collected the rubbish every Saturday
They added new plants to the park
They chose the problem for the class

aloud: I've been learning English since I was seven, and I think it's getting easier every year.
If the weather's nice on Friday, we're going to visit my grandparents in their village.

speak.prompt: Tell me about a trip or a special day you have enjoyed with your family. Where did you go, what did you do, and why did you enjoy it?
speak.expect: The learner can give a simple, connected narrative of a past experience in a linear sequence, using past simple accurately for most common verbs and linking ideas with basic connectors (first, then, after that, because, but, so). They can describe feelings and give brief reasons for their opinions (e.g. 'I liked it because...'). They use a sufficient range of everyday vocabulary (family, places, activities, food) with some circumlocution when a word is missing. Pauses for planning and repair are evident, and there are noticeable errors, especially in more complex structures, but meaning remains clear. Pronunciation is intelligible even with a noticeable accent, and the answer extends to several sentences rather than single words or isolated phrases.
